newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela gov't sees hope of averting Aug 6 strike.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela gov't sees hope of averting Aug 6 strike.

text.p: Venezuelan union, business and government leaders could reach an agreement on salary increases by Friday and avert a national strike called for August 6, Labor Minister Maria Bernardoni said Wednesday.
"We still have time to try to reach agreements in the tripartite commission which will satisfy the unions," Bernardoni said. "This could avert the unions' decision to call a national strike."
The Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), the nation's biggest union, called for a strike on August 6 to protest gasoline price increases and tardy salary rises.
Gasoline prices are due to increase 27 percent at midnight Wednesday.

The meeting Friday of tripartite commission members would seek to establish whether private sector companies had complied with a previous agreement to raise salaries after the reform of Venezuela's severance payments system last month, Bernardoni said.
Business chamber leaders have said that about 90 percent of their members had increased wages as agreed, while union leaders say less than 10 percent have done so.
"(The meeting) will allow us to have more accurate information about what each side is saying," Bernardoni said.
